dependency_inventory.description: Norm geometry baseline test vector from the metric operator baseline test vector pack; currently VALID_METADATA_VECTOR only; expected Lp distance fields not yet added.
The p parameter convention (explicit float64 vs. sentinel for p=inf) must be declared before the test vector schema can be finalized.
The canonical vector representation format (JSON array of float64 values) must be declared before fixture schema can be defined.

determinism_requirements: Lp norm distance is a closed-form expression with no iterative solver; it is fully deterministic given identical float64 vector inputs and an identical p parameter.
All element-wise absolute difference and power operations must be applied in a declared, stable traversal order (e.g., index 0 to n-1).
The summation order must be documented and fixed; the canonical order is left-to-right (index 0 to n-1).
No randomized or probabilistic algorithm components are permitted in the baseline plan.
All Lp norm computations must produce identical results across independent runs given identical inputs.

implementation_prerequisites.description: MetricOperatorRank4SelectionPlan.v1 must be present selecting NORM_GEOMETRY at rank 4 with SELECTION_PLAN_ONLY scope.
MetricOperatorRank4CandidateAudit.v1 must be present confirming NORM_GEOMETRY as the rank-4 candidate.
NormGeometryTestVectorSchemaPlan.v1 must be completed before fixture schema definitions can be created.

implementation_risks.description: Float64 overflow in the power step (|x_i - y_i|^p) for large element magnitudes or large p values; must be bounded by an input-magnitude policy before implementation.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Declare maximum allowed element magnitude and p value in the implementation plan; add NOT_COMPUTABLE branch for out-of-bound inputs.

implementation_risks.description: The p=inf sentinel convention must be fixed before implementation; ambiguous sentinel produces non-deterministic branch selection.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Declare canonical p=inf sentinel value (e.g., float('inf') or a string enum) in the data layout dependency before fixture schema is finalized.

implementation_risks.description: For general p, underflow of individual terms near zero may silently drop small contributions; documented bound required.
implementation_risks.mitigation: Define minimum non-zero element difference threshold in the implementation plan; add a note in validation requirements.

input_shape_requirements: Both input vectors (x and y) must be declared as finite, equal-length sequences of float64 values.
The dimension n must be >= 1; empty vector inputs (n = 0) must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
The p parameter must be a float64 value >= 1.0; values < 1.0 must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
Non-finite float64 values (NaN, +Inf, -Inf) in either vector must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE without distance computation.
Mismatched vector lengths (len(x) != len(y)) must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
Integer-valued vector inputs must be promoted to float64 before computation.
The p=inf case must be declared explicitly or inferred from a sentinel value; the implementation plan must declare which convention is used.
mathematical_requirements: The Lp norm distance between vectors x and y in R^n is defined as ||x - y||_p = (sum_i |x_i - y_i|^p)^(1/p) for p >= 1.
Special case p=1 (L1, Manhattan distance): ||x - y||_1 = sum_i |x_i - y_i|. Exact integer arithmetic is possible for integer-valued inputs; float64 required for the general case.
Special case p=2 (L2, Euclidean distance): ||x - y||_2 = sqrt(sum_i (x_i - y_i)^2). Float64 required; square root must use a stable float64 implementation.
Special case p=inf (Chebyshev distance): ||x - y||_inf = max_i |x_i - y_i|. Exact over float64 without a power or root operation.
For general p: the power operation (|x_i - y_i|^p) must use float64 throughout; no float32 intermediate values are permitted.
Vectors must have equal length (dimension n >= 1). Mismatched lengths are an invalid input and must be rejected before any distance computation begins.
Zero vector inputs (all elements 0.0) are valid; the distance between two identical zero vectors is 0.0.
The p parameter must satisfy p >= 1; values below 1.0 do not define a proper norm and must route to NOT_COMPUTABLE.
numerical_constraints: Float64 precision required for all intermediate computations including element-wise differences, powers, summation, and root extraction.
Float32 is excluded from the baseline plan.
Overflow risk: for large p values and large vector elements, |x_i - y_i|^p may overflow float64; the implementation plan must declare a bound on p and element magnitudes before implementation.
Underflow risk: for small differences and large p, individual terms may underflow to 0.0 prematurely; the implementation plan must address this before implementation.
No Lp norm computation is permitted during the planning phase.
numerical_stability_requirements: For p=2 (Euclidean), the square root must be computed with a float64 square root function; no approximation is permitted.
For general p, the (1/p) root must be computed with a float64 power function; the implementation plan must declare how the root is computed.
For p=inf, the maximum absolute difference must be computed without any power or root operation to avoid numerical loss.
Zero-difference inputs (x == y) must produce a distance of exactly 0.0 without any overflow or underflow in intermediate powers.
Very large element magnitudes (near float64 max) must not overflow in the power step; a documented input-magnitude policy is required before implementation.

validation_requirements.description: Baseline test vectors must be extended with norm-geometry-specific reference inputs (paired float64 vectors, p value) and pinned expected Lp distance scalars before implementation begins.
NOT_COMPUTABLE cases (empty vectors, mismatched lengths, p < 1, non-finite element values) must each have a dedicated validation fixture.
Deterministic replay validation: identical paired vector inputs and p must produce identical Lp distance output across independent runs.
Float64 precision validation: all intermediate computations must use float64; no float32 intermediate values permitted.
Special-case validation: p=1, p=2, and p=inf must each have dedicated reference fixtures with analytically exact expected values.
